source_text: Haec ergo gratia, quae in Baptismate non solum peccata condonat, sed cum hoc indulgentiae beneficio, et provehit, et adoptat, et consecrat; haec, inquam, gratia, meritum mutat reorum, non liberum condit arbitrium; quod eo accipimus tempore, quo creamur; utimur autem, quo valentiam inter bonum et malum discretionis adipiscimur. Bonae itaque voluntati innumeras adiutorii divini adesse species non negamus; sed ita ut non per adiutorii genera aut fabricetur, quae fuerit arbitrii destructa libertas, aut aliquando ea exclusa, vel boni vel mali cuiquam necessitas credatur incumbere; verum arbitrio libero omne adiutorium cooperatur.
pass_a_gloss: This grace therefore, which in Baptism not only condones sins, but with this benefit of indulgence, both advances, and adopts, and consecrates; this grace, I say, changes the desert of the guilty, does not found free choice; which we receive at that time, at which we are created; but we use, at which we obtain the strength of discretion between good and evil. We do not therefore deny that to a good will countless species of divine help are present; but so that not through the kinds of help either a liberty of choice which shall have been destroyed is fabricated, or at some time with it excluded, a necessity either of good or of evil is believed to lie upon anyone; but every help cooperates with free choice.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS libertas; Blaise moral freedom to will or refuse
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: This grace, then, which in baptism not only forgives sins but along with that gift of pardon also advances, adopts, and consecrates us, changes what the guilty deserve. It does not create free choice, which we receive when we are created and use when we acquire the power to distinguish good and evil. We therefore do not deny that countless forms of divine help assist a good will. But this does not mean that these forms of help construct a freedom of choice that had been destroyed, or that at some time freedom is excluded and a necessity of either good or evil is thought to lie upon anyone. Rather, every help cooperates with free choice.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
